THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

260-Calorie Toasted Roast Beef & Cheese Sandwich

Quick Lunches Ep. 2 — hot roast beef, melted Velveeta, toasted Sola bread, mustard. 260 cal / 34g protein in about six minutes.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME2 min prep + 6 min Air Fry
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~260 cal | ~34g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Air Fry mode 5–6 minutes. Temperature is not published — your air fryer's Air Fry preset handles it. Appliance settings vary.

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 3 oz deli roast beef
  • 1 slice Velveeta Original (or any pasteurized prepared cheese slice)
  • 2 slices Sola Sweet & Buttery bread (or any high-fiber sandwich bread)
  • Yellow mustard, to taste

Allergens: dairy, wheat. Packaged labels vary — verify current bread, cheese, and roast beef packages before publishing allergen or gluten free tags. Formulations drift. No temperature published for Air Fry step — appliance settings vary. Follow the physical package for definitive heating guidance.

You want a hot roast beef sandwich in under 10 minutes without pulling out a skillet. 34g protein at 260 cal — the whole sandwich is one entrée, not a snack. Second episode of the Quick Lunches numbered series.

Method

  1. 1.PORTION BEEF. Lay 3 oz deli roast beef on a sheet of air-fryer-safe parchment. Loose folds, not stacked flat — helps the cheese melt into the layers instead of sliding off.
  2. 2.ADD CHEESE. Place 1 slice of Velveeta directly on top of the beef. The beef acts as the heat carrier; the cheese melts passively as the beef warms.
  3. 3.AIR FRY. Run Air Fry mode for 5–6 minutes until the beef is hot throughout and the cheese fully melted. Do not invent a temperature — use your air fryer's Air Fry preset. Appliance settings vary.
  4. 4.TOAST BREAD. While the beef and cheese are in the air fryer, toast 2 slices of Sola Sweet & Buttery bread to your preferred crispness. Watch closely — low-carb bread browns fast at the edges.
  5. 5.BUILD. Transfer the hot roast beef and melted cheese onto one slice of toast in a single scoop with the parchment. Add yellow mustard to taste.
  6. 6.FINISH. Close the sandwich, slice on the diagonal, serve immediately. The bread stays crisp; the cheese stays molten.

Keys to success

  • Beef and cheese cook TOGETHER on parchment. Stacking cheese on beef before the air fryer is what starts the melt — reversing the order gives you cold cheese on hot beef.
  • Toast the bread in parallel, not sequentially. If you wait until the beef is done to start the toast, the beef cools while the bread crisps.

If something fails

Bread over-browned before beef finished: Toaster ran ahead. Wait 60-90 sec after starting the air fryer before dropping bread in the toaster — the beef needs the full 5-6 min head start.

Cheese didn't fully melt: Beef wasn't hot enough OR cheese slice was cold from the fridge. Let the Velveeta sit at room temp for 2 min before assembly, and confirm the beef is steaming when it comes out.

Sandwich fell apart when sliced: Sliced too soon or too aggressively. Let it rest 30 seconds after closing so the cheese re-firms slightly, then slice diagonally with a serrated knife.

Not filling enough: Add another slice of toast + one more oz of roast beef (~90 cal / 8g protein). Or pair with a broth cup or side salad. The sandwich itself is intentionally lean.

Mustard overwhelms the beef: Yellow mustard is sharp — start with 1 tsp and taste. Dijon reads milder if yellow's tang is too aggressive.

Storage and reheating

Store: Best assembled and eaten immediately. If prepping components, keep bread, roast beef, cheese, and mustard separate.

Reheat: N/A — assemble hot. Follow the roast beef package if reheating a stored cooked portion.

Lasts: Assembled = same-meal only. Components hold per each package's own storage guidance.

~260 cal | ~34g protein.

Watch the full cook

Brands I use

Sola
Sweet & Buttery Bread (~40 cal / 5g protein per slice)
Two slices at ~80 cal / 10g protein is what makes 34g total feasible without a second protein ingredient. Toasts crisp without going stiff; holds up to hot filling.
Velveeta
Original Slices (35 cal per slice)
Melts fastest under passive beef heat without a second cook step. Full slice at 35 cal keeps the sandwich under 260 cal while giving the beef a proper cheese pull.
Boar's Head / Deli-Counter
Deli Roast Beef (~90 cal / 22g protein per 3 oz)
Lean deli roast beef is the anchor. The specific brand wasn't required — any oven-roasted deli beef sliced thin works. Verify sodium if that matters for your household.
French's
Classic Yellow Mustard (5 cal per tsp)
Standard yellow mustard. Any brand works — French's is what's filmed and stocks the pantry cheapest.
